summary: Witaszek proves Keel's base point free theorem for schemes projective over an excellent mixed-characteristic base: a nef line bundle is semiample (or EWM) if and only if it is so on its exceptional locus and on the characteristic-zero fibre (Theorem 1.2). Its tools are a mixed-characteristic analogue of Kollár's quotients by finite equivalence relations (Theorem 1.4) and pushouts along universal homeomorphisms via perfection (Theorem 1.7). Applications include the base point free theorem for klt threefolds over mixed-characteristic Dedekind bases (Corollary 6.7). Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and fourteen findings are recorded. Lemma 2.1 needs surjectivity (E2); Keel's surface lemma, and the paper's paraphrase of it, need h⁰ ≥ 2 (E5); the introduction overstates Corollary 6.7 (E3); the main theorems stand. Not formalised.

items.statement: For X separated finite type over Noetherian S, σ₁,σ₂:E⇒X are finite and E→X×S X is injective on points valued in every algebraically closed field, with equivalence-relation image. Nilpotents in E are allowed; the map need not be a monomorphism.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

api.statement: Project the two finite maps and injectivity on geometric points.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.finite_equivalence.api2

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.finite_equivalence.api3
api.statement: Pull back the geometric relation and distinguish reduction of its scheme structure.

items.name: Geometric quotient of a finite relation
items.statement: A categorical coequalizer X→Y in separated finite-type S-algebraic spaces is geometric if finite and its geometric-point fibers are exactly the equivalence classes.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.finite_geometric_quotient.api2

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.finite_geometric_quotient.api3
api.statement: Use finiteness and target category as explicit fields.

items.name: Integral-relative quotient
items.statement: If X is separated finite type over Noetherian S, X→Y integral, and E⇒X a finite equivalence relation over Y, its geometric quotient exists.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Proper group action
items.statement: For an affine group scheme G of finite type over Noetherian S acting on X, properness means (m,p₂):G×S X→X×S X is proper.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Topological quotient of a proper action
items.statement: A G-invariant map q:X→Z is a topological quotient if locally of finite type, universally submersive, and induces the orbit-space bijection on all algebraically closed-field points.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.topological_action_quotient.api1
api.statement: Expose invariance and geometric orbit fibers.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.topological_action_quotient.api2

api.statement: Compare with the geometric quotient by its additional invariant-sheaf property.

items.name: Geometric quotient of a proper action
items.statement: A topological quotient is geometric if O_Z→(q_*O_X)^G is an isomorphism.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Invariant relative spectrum upgrades a quotient
items.statement: For flat affine finite-type G over Noetherian S with proper action, a topological quotient q:X→Z gives a geometric quotient Spec_Z((q_*O_X)^G), finite universally homeomorphic over Z.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Proper affine actions have finite action graph
items.statement: For an affine finite-type group with proper action, the action graph is finite; geometric quotients are affine and separated, and for X finite type their targets are finite type.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Proper-action geometric quotient is categorical
items.statement: A geometric quotient of a proper action has the categorical quotient universal property.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Finite equivariant maps descend to quotient maps
items.statement: If a finite equivariant map of proper G-spaces has geometric quotients at both ends, the induced quotient map is finite, and is a universal homeomorphism if the original map is.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Topological pushout datum
items.statement: Given Y→pX and Y→gY′ with p representable quasi-compact quasi-separated and g representable universal homeomorphism, a topological pushout is a commuting square with X→fX′ representable universal homeomorphism. The terminology alone does not assert a categorical pushout.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.topological_pushout.api1
api.statement: Project the commuting square and representable universal-homeomorphism f.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.topological_pushout.api2
api.statement: Base change the square without asserting ring-sheaf equality.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.topological_pushout.api3
api.statement: Attach the geometric refinement as a separate construction.

items.name: Geometric pushout
items.statement: A topological pushout is geometric if O_X′→f_*O_X ×_(fp)_*O_Y q_*O_Y′ is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.geometric_pushout.api1
api.statement: Expose the ring-sheaf fiber-product isomorphism.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.geometric_pushout.api2
api.statement: Supply the categorical pushout lift and uniqueness via Lemma2.25.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.geometric_pushout.api3
api.statement: Use flat base-change and étale-local descent comparisons.

items.name: Affine fiber-product criterion
items.statement: For affine input rings A→B←B′, if Spec B→Spec B′ and Spec A→Spec(A×B B′) are universal homeomorphisms, Spec(A×B B′) is the geometric pushout.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Morphisms and separation in a pushout
items.statement: In a topological pushout, q is representable quasi-compact quasi-separated; if p is separated, affine, universally closed or integral then so is q. Quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness and separation of X pass to X′. In a geometric pushout, injectivity of g# implies injectivity of f#.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Refinement of a topological pushout
items.statement: Any topological pushout admits a geometric refinement over its target by relative Spec of the fiber-product algebra; the comparison is a universal homeomorphism.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Geometric pushout may be non-Noetherian
items.statement: The pushout of Spec Z←Spec Q→Spec(Q[ε]/ε²) has coordinate ring Z⊕Qε with ε²=0, which is not Noetherian.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Finite-type topological approximation
items.statement: If X is finite type over Noetherian S and its input diagram has a topological pushout, there is one finite type over S; if X is proper, it can be chosen proper. No assertion that this approximation is geometric.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Flat base change of geometric pushouts
items.statement: Flat base change of a geometric pushout is a geometric pushout.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Étale transport of a pushout
items.statement: For compatible input diagrams linked by Cartesian étale maps, a geometric pushout for the lower diagram pulls back to a geometric pushout of the upper diagram and an étale target map.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Geometric pushout is categorical
items.statement: A geometric pushout satisfies the categorical pushout universal property in algebraic spaces (and in schemes when all objects are schemes).
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Local existence of geometric pushouts
items.statement: Existence is Zariski local on X for schemes and étale local on X for algebraic spaces.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Conductor square for a finite reduced surjection
items.statement: For finite surjective f:Y→X of reduced Noetherian schemes, define the conductor I locally as {s∈B:sB⊆A} for A⊆B. It is an ideal in both rings and A=B×_(B/I)(A/I); this does not require birationality.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim. Mathlib's conductor A (0:B) already supplies the affine ideal; only scheme gluing, localization comparison and the square are missing.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.conductor_square.api1
api.statement: Expose the largest B-ideal contained in A.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.conductor_square.api2
api.statement: Give the ring isomorphism A≅B×_(B/I)(A/I).

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.conductor_square.api3
api.statement: Glue localization-compatible ideals and recover the closed conductor subschemes.

items.name: Rank-one Milnor patching
items.statement: For a ring fiber product A=B×D C with C→D surjective, finite projective modules are equivalent to compatible finite-projective pairs; the equivalence restricts to rank-one modules and their isomorphisms.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Picard groupoids of conductor squares
items.statement: For the conductor square C→X, D→Y above, Pic(X)→Pic(Y)×Pic(D)Pic(C) is an equivalence of groupoids (2-fiber product).
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Direct-limit multiplicative perfection
items.statement: For a commutative monoid M and prime p, M^perf is the filtered colimit M→M→… of p-th powers. Applied to a Z_(p)-algebra this forgets addition; p-th power is not a mixed-characteristic ring map.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.multiplicative_perfection.api1
api.statement: Use classes [a,n] with [a,n]=[a^p,n+1].

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.multiplicative_perfection.api2
api.statement: Expose the eventual-power equality test.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.multiplicative_perfection.api3
api.statement: Lift compatible power-diagram maps uniquely and compare finite limits.

items.name: Equality in the perfection
items.statement: Two representatives [a,n],[b,m] agree iff for some N≥n,m, a^(p^(N−n))=b^(p^(N−m)). In particular the kernel of M→M^perf is eventual equality of p-powers.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Perfection preserves fiber products
items.statement: For commutative monoid maps A→B←C, (A×B C)^perf→A^perf×B^perf C^perf is an isomorphism.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Filtered colimits commute with finite limits
items.statement: The abstract concrete-category theorem supplies preservation of finite limits by filtered colimits under its stated forgetful-functor preservation/reflection hypotheses.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim. Actual pinned declaration statement read; API beyond that statement is a planning interface, not claimed built.

items.name: Perfection of a line-bundle sheaf
items.statement: For L on a Z_(p)-scheme, L^perf is the sheafification of the set-presheaf colimit of L^(p^n) under p-th powers of sections. Define H⁰(X,L)^perf as the analogous colimit of global-section sets.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.line_perfection.api1
api.statement: Expose local identifications with perfected coordinate monoids after trivialization.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.line_perfection.api2
api.statement: Compare qcqs global sections with the direct limit of section sets.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.line_perfection.api3
api.statement: Transport across line-bundle isomorphisms and tensor powers.

items.name: Quasi-compact quasi-separated global sections
items.statement: For quasi-compact quasi-separated X, H⁰(X,L^perf) identifies with H⁰(X,L)^perf.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Uniform binomial divisibility
items.statement: For prime p, n≥1 and k≥n−1, p^n divides p^i binomial(p^k,i) for every 1≤i≤p^k. For n,N≥1, m≥n+floor(log_p N) ensures p^n divides binomial(p^m,i) for 1≤i≤N.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Integral rational isomorphism gives eventual powers
items.statement: If B→A is integral, a universal homeomorphism, and an isomorphism after inverting p, every a∈A has some p-power in the image of B.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Kernel torsion gives eventual equal powers
items.statement: Under the preceding hypotheses, if b,b′∈B have equal images in A, some common p-power of b,b′ is equal in B.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Infinitesimal invariance up to multiplicative perfection
items.statement: For affine f:X→Y over Z_(p) with f_Q an isomorphism, O_Y^perf→f_*O_X^perf is an isomorphism iff f is a universal homeomorphism.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Perfection pullback along a universal homeomorphism
items.statement: For a universal homeomorphism f:X→Y over Z_(p), the structure-sheaf perfection square for X,Y and X_Q,Y_Q is Cartesian.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Perfected section pullback
items.statement: For universal homeomorphism f:X→Y of quasi-compact quasi-separated Z_(p)-schemes and L on Y, the square of H⁰(−,L)^perf over X,Y,X_Q,Y_Q is Cartesian.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Picard groupoid
items.statement: Pic(X) has line bundles as objects and only isomorphisms as morphisms. It is the core of the existing full invertible-sheaf category, not the Picard group of isomorphism classes.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.picard_groupoid.api1
api.statement: Include only invertible morphisms from the full line-bundle category.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.picard_groupoid.api2
api.statement: Expose tensor product, unit, dual and pullback as groupoid functors.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.picard_groupoid.api3
api.statement: Identify Aut(O_X) with global units and π₀ with the Picard group.

items.name: Picard groupoid with formal p-power roots
items.statement: Pic(X)[1/p] has objects (L,n), n∈N, and Hom((L,n),(M,m))=colim_(N≥n,m) Isom(L^(p^(N−n)),M^(p^(N−m))).
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

api.statement: Construct formal-root objects (L,n).

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.picard_invert_p.api2
api.statement: Compose morphism representatives at a common sufficiently large exponent.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.picard_invert_p.api3
api.statement: Give the comparison Pic(X)→Pic(X)[1/p] and the formal p-power-root equivalence.

items.name: Characteristic-p universal homeomorphism descent
items.statement: For finite universal homeomorphism of Noetherian F_p-schemes, pullback gives an equivalence of Picard groupoids after inverting p.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Rational Picard square for a thickening
items.statement: For a finite thickening X→Y of Noetherian Z_(p)-schemes, Pic(Y)[1/p]→Pic(X)[1/p]×Pic(X_Q)[1/p]Pic(Y_Q)[1/p] is an equivalence.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Reduction step for the rational Picard square
items.statement: The rational Picard-square assertion for a finite universal homeomorphism of Noetherian Z_(p)-schemes follows from the assertion for its reductions.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Rationalized Picard descent across finite universal homeomorphisms
items.statement: For finite universal homeomorphism X→Y of Noetherian Z_(p)-schemes, the Pic(−)[1/p] square with rational fibers is 2-Cartesian.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Unit groups retain the rational square
items.statement: The same square is Cartesian on unit groups after inverting p; it is obtained from automorphisms of the trivial object, not merely from π₀Pic.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Picard comparison for finite topological pushouts
items.statement: For a topological pushout of Noetherian Z_(p)-algebraic spaces satisfying Definition2.17, with both horizontal universal homeomorphisms finite, the square whose top row is Pic(X′)→Pic(X)×Pic(Y)Pic(Y′) and bottom row is its rational-fiber analogue is 2-Cartesian after inverting p. Neither row is asserted to be an equivalence by itself.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Arithmetic fiber product is universally homeomorphic
items.statement: For a ring B, B′=B⊗ZQ and a universal-homeomorphism map A′→B′ of Q-algebras, A=B×B′A′→B induces a universal homeomorphism.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Pushout from the rational fiber
items.statement: For X and a representable universal homeomorphism X_Q→X′_Q, X⊔X_QX′_Q exists geometrically, in schemes or algebraic spaces as appropriate.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Arithmetic specificity of the pushout argument
items.statement: Replacing Z⊂Q by C[t]⊂C(t) does not give the same finite-type behavior: B=C[t][x,y], A′=C(t)[x²,x³,x+ty] leads after quotient to C[t][ty,ty²,…], not finitely generated.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Mixed-characteristic pushout theorem
items.statement: For Y→pX representable quasi-compact separated and Y→gY′ representable universal homeomorphism, if the rational-fiber diagram admits a topological pushout, the original diagram admits a geometric pushout. Schemes stay schemes.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Universal-homeomorphism coequalizer
items.statement: Let R→E⇒X have R→E representable universal homeomorphism, E⇒X representable quasi-compact quasi-separated, equal on R. If the rational diagram has a universal-homeomorphism coequalizer, so does the original diagram; require X qcqs for algebraic spaces, not for the scheme version.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Finite pinching
items.statement: For Noetherian algebraic spaces X,Z,V over Noetherian S, a closed immersion Z→X and finite surjection Z→V have a universal pushout Y, Noetherian, with V→Y closed, Z=X×YV, X→Y finite and an isomorphism off V. If the inputs are finite type over S, so is Y.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Ample descent along finite surjections
items.statement: For finite surjective Y→X of proper schemes over a Noetherian affine base, L is ample iff its pullback is ample.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Relative ample invertible sheaf
items.statement: Use the upstream relative ampleness and projectivity interface; finite-type relative Proj and a generating power define the polarized contraction.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim. Imported scope from the named layer, not replanned here.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.ample.api1
api.statement: Use the upstream relative ampleness predicate and local affine-base criterion.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.ample.api2
api.statement: Pull back along arbitrary base changes.

api.name: MixedCharacteristic.ample.api3
api.statement: Positive tensor powers preserve and reflect relative ampleness.

Supplies Relative ample invertible sheaf with its stated hypotheses to Polarized contraction associated to a semiample bundle.

Supplies Relative ample invertible sheaf with its stated hypotheses to Serre vanishing and section lifting.

items.name: Polarized contraction associated to a semiample bundle
items.statement: Over a Noetherian base, a relatively semiample line bundle on a projective scheme has, after a positive power, a proper contraction to a projective target pulling back an ample bundle.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: EWM gluing across two closed pieces
items.statement: For reduced projective X=X₁∪X₂ over Noetherian S, if L|X₁,L|X₂,L|X_Q are EWM and the associated map on X₂ has geometrically connected fibers on X₁∩X₂, then L is EWM.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Semiampleness gluing across two closed pieces
items.statement: Under the same reduced/projective/Noetherian setup, if the three restrictions are semiample and the intersection map has geometrically connected fibers, L is semiample.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: EWM gluing from normalization and conductor
items.statement: Let X be reduced projective over excellent S, Y its normalization, C⊂X,D⊂Y its conductors. If pullback L on Y, L|C and L|X_Q are EWM and the Y contraction restricted to D has geometrically connected fibers, L is EWM.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Semiampleness gluing from normalization
items.statement: Under the preceding hypotheses with semiample in place of EWM, L is semiample.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: EWM gluing with finitely many disconnected fibers
items.statement: Proposition5.1 remains true when all geometric fibers of the intersection map are connected except finitely many over closed points.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Conductor EWM gluing with finite exceptions
items.statement: The EWM part of Proposition5.2 permits finitely many disconnected geometric fibers over closed points.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Semiampleness gluing with finite exceptions
items.statement: The semiample part of Proposition5.1 permits finitely many disconnected geometric fibers over closed points if positive-characteristic closed residue fields of S are locally finite.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Conductor semiampleness gluing with finite exceptions
items.statement: The semiample part of Proposition5.2 permits finitely many disconnected geometric fibers over closed points under the same locally finite residue-field assumption.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: EWM detected by reduction and rational fiber
items.statement: For nef L on X projective over Noetherian S, L is EWM iff L|X_red and L|X_Q are EWM.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Semiampleness detected by reduction and rational fiber
items.statement: For nef L on X projective over Noetherian S, L is semiample iff L|X_red and L|X_Q are semiample.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Uniform Fujita vanishing
items.statement: For X projective over Noetherian A, ample H and coherent F, there is m₀ such that H^q(X,F⊗H^m⊗N)=0 for every m≥m₀, q>0 and nef N.
items.locator: Keeler03 Theorem1.5, with 2018 corrigendum E2.5; Theorem6.1 proof
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Mixed-characteristic Keel semiampleness
items.statement: For X projective over excellent S and relatively nef L, L is relatively semiample iff its restrictions to E(L) and X_Q are relatively semiample.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Mixed-characteristic Keel EWM
items.statement: For X projective over S, where S is of finite type over a mixed-characteristic Dedekind domain, and nef L, L is EWM iff its restrictions to E(L) and X_Q are EWM.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Finite quotients from reduction and rational fiber
items.statement: For finite equivalence E⇒X with X separated finite type over Noetherian S, if quotients exist for the reduced relation and rational fiber, the geometric quotient X/E exists.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Normal pure-dimensional finite relation quotient
items.statement: For a finite set-theoretic equivalence R⇒X with X normal Noetherian and both X,R pure-dimensional, if X is essentially of finite type over the Noetherian base S, the geometric quotient exists as a normal Noetherian algebraic space essentially of finite type over S. This is case(2) of Kollár12 Lemma21; its two other alternatives are separate source variants.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Reduction of a relation after its maximal-dimensional quotient
items.statement: After quotienting the maximal-dimensional part on a normal pure-dimensional space, the remaining nontrivial relation is supported on a proper lower-dimensional closed subset; finite pullback/pushforward of relations gives the compatible quotient data.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Finite set-theoretic quotients in mixed characteristic
items.statement: For X separated finite type over excellent S and finite set-theoretic equivalence relation E⇒X, if X_Q/E_Q exists, then the geometric quotient X/E exists as a separated finite-type algebraic space.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Quotient descent along a finite equivariant universal homeomorphism
items.statement: For flat affine finite-type G over Noetherian S, proper actions on separated finite-type X,Y, and finite equivariant universal homeomorphism X→Y, existence of Y/G implies existence of X/G.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Quotient ascent with a rational quotient
items.statement: In the same setup, existence of X/G and Y_Q/G_Q implies existence of Y/G.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Normal proper-action quotient
items.statement: A smooth affine finite-type group over an excellent base acting properly on a normal separated finite-type space has a normal finite-type geometric quotient.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Seminormal conductor descent for proper actions
items.statement: The seminormalization and conductor-reduction step required by Witaszek's Theorem1.5 must provide equivariant finite conductor data and quotient gluing from normalization and lower-dimensional conductor quotients.
items.locator: Theorem1.5 proof; Kollár97 Corollary5.6/Theorem5.8 as cited
items.note: Interface obligation only: exact original formulation is unresolved, not a verified theorem claim.

items.name: Geometric quotients for proper smooth affine-group actions
items.statement: For excellent S, smooth affine finite-type G over S acting properly on separated finite-type X, a geometric quotient X/G exists and is separated finite type over S.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Changing the acting group by a universal homeomorphism
items.statement: For a universal homeomorphism G′→G of flat finite-type groups over Noetherian S acting properly, global geometric-quotient existence for G and G′ is equivalent if both rational quotients exist.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Degree of a line bundle on a proper curve
items.statement: Use the existing planned divisor/line-bundle degree over the field of constants of an integral proper curve; in Lemma6.8 the field is H⁰(F,O_F), not automatically the original residue field.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim. Imported scope from the named layer, not replanned here.

items.name: Coherent cohomology under proper maps
items.statement: For proper f:X→S of Noetherian schemes and coherent F, R^if_*F is coherent; over a field its global cohomology is finite dimensional. Flat base change gives the corresponding cohomology comparison.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim. Imported scope from the named layer, not replanned here.

items.name: Serre vanishing and section lifting
items.statement: For X projective over Noetherian affine S, ample A and coherent F, H^i(X,F⊗A^n)=0 for i>0 and n sufficiently large; in particular restrictions of high ample powers to a fixed closed subscheme are surjective on sections.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Nef top intersection detects bigness
items.statement: For integral d-dimensional proper variety over a field and nef L, bigness is equivalent to (L^d)>0; a finite surjective f of degree e satisfies (f*L)^d=e(L^d).
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Affine–contraction–affine factorization
items.statement: For a quasi-compact separated morphism Y→X with X affine, the compactification theorem plus Stein factorization supplies Y→X₁→X₀→X with outer maps affine and middle map a contraction.
items.note: Exact source proof closure open; this records the needed factorization, not a verified reading of Temkin.

items.name: Formal contraction algebraization required for EWM
items.statement: In Theorem6.1's big-component setup over a base of finite type over an excellent Dedekind domain, the compatible contractions on thickenings of D, with the vanishing supplied there, algebraize to an algebraic-space contraction.
items.locator: Theorem6.1 EWM proof; Artin70 Theorems3.1,6.2; Keel99 Proposition1.6
items.note: Interface obligation; primary Artin statements and proof not yet read, so exact closure is explicitly open.

items.name: Numerically trivial bundles are EWM over a field
items.statement: A nef numerically trivial bundle on a proper connected variety over a field is EWM with the constant map; positive-dimensional integral subvarieties are precisely those contracted, while restrictions to points are big.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Numerically trivial bundles over locally finite fields
items.statement: For a projective scheme over an algebraic extension of a finite field, a numerically trivial line bundle is torsion and hence semiample.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Numerically trivial Picard classes form finite-type components
items.statement: For a projective scheme over a field, the numerically trivial Picard functor is represented by a finite-type group scheme, allowing descent to finite fields and finiteness of rational classes.
items.note: Source-scoped interface only; Picard representability and numerical boundedness need original-source closure.

items.name: Generic Q-trivial nef divisors descend relatively
items.statement: For a projective contraction f:X→Y of normal excellent integral schemes, Y Q-factorial, L nef Q-Cartier and generically Q-trivial, if each prime divisor of X dominates Y or maps to a prime divisor, L is Q-linearly equivalent to a pullback from Y.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Log pair and discrepancy conventions
items.statement: A log pair (X,Δ) here consists of normal integral excellent finite-dimensional X with the required dualizing/canonical-divisor data, effective rational Weil divisor Δ and K_X+Δ Q-Cartier. For a divisorial valuation E on a birational model, use coefficient a(E;X,Δ) in K_Y−f*(K_X+Δ).
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.statement: For the log-pair convention, klt means a(E;X,Δ)>−1 for every divisorial valuation including components on X. Plt permits boundary components of coefficient1, with coefficients≤1 and discrepancies>−1 for exceptional divisorial valuations.

items.statement: For the divisors D_i and Γ_i of Corollary6.7, normalization D̄_i carries effective Δ_D̄_i with (K_X+D_i+Γ_i)|D̄_i∼QK_D̄_i+Δ_D̄_i; the one-dimensional conductor and previously added boundary curves occur in Supp floor(Δ_D̄_i).

items.name: Characteristic-zero base-point-free input
items.statement: For the projective characteristic-zero fibers of the klt/plt pairs in Section6.4, the nef Cartier bundle satisfying the stated ample, respectively nef-and-big adjoint difference is semiample.
items.note: Primary-source reading and its transitive vanishing/resolution inputs remain open.

items.name: Excellent-surface abundance input for plt adjunction
items.statement: For the normal divisor D in Corollary6.5 with its adjunction pair, Tanaka's excellent-surface MMP/abundance results imply semiampleness of the restricted adjoint-nef bundle.
items.note: Source-scoped interface obligation, not a verified full Tanaka theorem statement.

items.name: Plt threefold contraction
items.statement: Let S be quasi-projective over a mixed-characteristic Dedekind domain. For a plt pair (X,D+B), X normal integral of absolute dimension3 projective over S, D normal irreducible, B effective rational, and nef Cartier L with L−(K_X+D+B) ample and E(L)⊆D, L is semiample.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Relative surface EWM
items.statement: In Section6.4's base convention, let normal integral X of absolute dimension2 be projective over S with dim π(X)≥1. If L is nef and semiample on the generic fiber of its image, L is EWM.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Relative surface semiampleness
items.statement: Under Proposition6.6's preceding hypotheses, if positive-characteristic closed residue fields of S are locally finite, L is semiample.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Uniform top cohomology bound for nef powers
items.statement: For a projective pure-dimensional d-dimensional scheme X over a field and nef line bundle L, h^d(X,L^m) is bounded for m≥1.
items.note: Narrowed to the actual Keel99 Lemma5.4 statement required here. The old arbitrary-coherent-F top-cohomology assertion was an unverified strengthening; the auxiliary statement in Keel’s proof instead bounds h⁰(F⊗L^(−m)).

items.name: Linear Euler growth in the numerical-dimension-one case
items.statement: For a normalized surface component in Corollary6.7 over an algebraically closed field, nef ν(L)=1 and aL≡K+Δ+A with effective Δ and ample A imply χ(L^m)=χ(O)+cm with c>0. The H² bound gives h⁰(L^m)≥χ(O)+cm−C and hence a moving positive power.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Nef abundant numerical-dimension-one surface bundle
items.statement: On a normal projective surface over an algebraically closed field, a nef line bundle with numerical dimension1 and Iitaka dimension1 is semiample.
items.locator: Guarded input for Corollary6.7; compare Keel99 Lemma5.2
items.note: Retains the cc-fb70e5 fibration repair; codex-c83e7a makes the stronger moving-section hypothesis and smooth-resolution step explicit.

items.name: Conductor has at most one geometric point generically
items.statement: In Corollary6.7's numerical-dimension-one case, the reduced conductor on the generic fiber F of D̄_i→Z_i is empty or supported on one geometric point. The same bound applies to the reduced inverse image of the previously glued boundary.
items.locator: Lemma6.8 and final proof paragraph, guarded formulation
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Klt threefold EWM over a mixed-characteristic Dedekind base
items.statement: For klt (X,Δ), X normal integral of absolute dimension3, projective and surjective over Spec of a mixed-characteristic Dedekind domain with PERFECT closed residue fields, nef and big Cartier L with L−(K_X+Δ) nef and big is EWM.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim. (cc-442dc5) The introduction's broader sentence without perfect residue fields is finding E3.

items.name: Klt threefold semiampleness over locally finite residues
items.statement: Under Corollary6.7's hypotheses, if positive-characteristic closed residue fields are locally finite, L is semiample.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Numerical dimension of a nef surface bundle
items.statement: For nef L on a projective integral surface, ν(L)=2 if L²>0; otherwise ν(L)=1 if L has positive intersection with some curve, and ν(L)=0 if numerically trivial.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Iitaka dimension
items.statement: For L on an integral projective variety, κ(L)=−∞ when every positive power has no nonzero section; otherwise it is the maximum dimension of the images of the rational maps of nonempty complete linear systems |L^m|.

items.name: Locally finite field
items.statement: A locally finite field is an algebraic extension of a finite field; equivalently every finitely generated subfield is finite.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Built ring conductor ideal
items.statement: For a commutative R-algebra B and b∈B, conductor R b is the largest B-ideal contained in the subalgebra R[b]. For an injective A→B, choosing b=0 gives the conductor of the image of A.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Eventual powers yield a spectrum homeomorphism
items.statement: For a ring homomorphism f:R→B with ker f contained in the nilradical and every b∈B having some positive power in image f, Spec(f) is a homeomorphism.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Purely inseparable field extension after arbitrary ring base change
items.statement: For a purely inseparable field extension K/k and any commutative k-algebra R, Spec(R⊗kK)→Spec R is a homeomorphism.
items.note: Source-scoped planning item; not an implementation claim.

items.name: Purely inseparable and separable extensions are trivial
items.statement: For fields F,E with an F-algebra structure, if E/F is purely inseparable and separable, algebraMap F E is bijective.
items.note: Continuation proof decomposition; mathematical outline only, no Lean implementation claim.

items.name: Characteristic-zero radicial residue extensions are trivial
items.statement: A purely inseparable field extension E/F with char F=0 has bijective algebraMap, hence is an F-algebra isomorphism.
items.note: Continuation proof decomposition; mathematical outline only, no Lean implementation claim.

items.name: Smooth projective surface Riemann–Roch supplier
items.statement: For a smooth projective integral surface T over an algebraically closed field and Cartier divisor D, χ(O_T(D))=χ(O_T)+(D²−D·K_T)/2.
items.locator: Published pp.700–701; Keel99 pp.280–282, expanded continuation argument
items.note: Continuation proof decomposition; mathematical outline only, no Lean implementation claim.

items.name: Projective resolution of a normal surface
items.statement: A normal projective integral surface over an algebraically closed field admits a projective birational morphism π:T→S, isomorphic over the regular locus, with T smooth projective.
items.locator: Published pp.700–701; Keel99 pp.280–282, expanded continuation argument
items.note: Continuation proof decomposition; mathematical outline only, no Lean implementation claim.

items.name: Sections and semiampleness under a normal surface resolution
items.statement: For the preceding π and a line bundle L on S, π_*O_T=O_S, H⁰(S,L^m)≅H⁰(T,π*L^m) for all m, and L is semiample iff π*L is semiample.
items.locator: Published pp.700–701; Keel99 pp.280–282, expanded continuation argument
items.note: Continuation proof decomposition; mathematical outline only, no Lean implementation claim.

items.name: Resolution correction to Euler characteristic is constant
items.statement: For π:T→S as above and a line bundle L, χ(S,L^m)−χ(T,π*L^m)=χ(S,O_S)−χ(T,O_T) for all integers m.
items.locator: Published pp.700–701; Keel99 pp.280–282, expanded continuation argument
items.note: Continuation proof decomposition; mathematical outline only, no Lean implementation claim.

items.name: Cartier Riemann–Roch on a normal projective surface
items.statement: For normal projective integral S over an algebraically closed field and Cartier L, χ(S,L^m)=χ(S,O_S)+(m²L²−m L·K_S)/2. Intersections with the Weil canonical divisor are Cartier–Weil intersections.
items.locator: Published pp.700–701; Keel99 pp.280–282, expanded continuation argument
items.note: Continuation proof decomposition; mathematical outline only, no Lean implementation claim.

items.name: Adjunction forces a positive Euler slope
items.statement: On such S, let L be nef with ν(L)=1 and suppose aL≡K_S+Δ+A, with a>0, Δ effective Q-Weil and A ample Q-Cartier. Then c=−L·K_S/2=(L·Δ+L·A)/2>0.
items.locator: Published pp.700–701; Keel99 pp.280–282, expanded continuation argument
items.note: Continuation proof decomposition; mathematical outline only, no Lean implementation claim.

items.name: A positive Euler slope and bounded H² force moving sections
items.statement: If χ(S,L^m)=χ(O_S)+cm with c>0 and h²(S,L^m)≤C for m≥1, then h⁰(S,L^m)≥χ(O_S)+cm−C. In particular some positive power has at least two independent sections.
items.locator: Published pp.700–701; Keel99 pp.280–282, expanded continuation argument
items.note: Continuation proof decomposition; mathematical outline only, no Lean implementation claim.

items.name: Intersection matrix of a connected fibre
items.statement: For a morphism f:T→C from a smooth projective surface to a smooth projective curve with connected fibres, write f*(t)=Σm_i C_i, m_i>0. Its component intersection form is negative semidefinite, with kernel exactly Q·(m_i).
items.locator: Published pp.700–701; Keel99 pp.280–282, expanded continuation argument
items.note: Continuation proof decomposition; mathematical outline only, no Lean implementation claim.

items.name: A vertical effective divisor of square zero comes from the base
items.statement: For f:T→C as above and effective vertical Q-divisor F with F²=0, F=Σ_t q_t f*(t) with q_t≥0 rational and finite support.
items.locator: Published pp.700–701; Keel99 pp.280–282, expanded continuation argument
items.note: Continuation proof decomposition; mathematical outline only, no Lean implementation claim.

items.name: A nef numerical-dimension-one bundle with moving sections is semiample
items.statement: On a normal projective surface over an algebraically closed field, if L is nef, ν(L)=1, and h⁰(S,L^m)≥2 for some m>0, then L is semiample.
items.locator: Published pp.700–701; Keel99 pp.280–282, expanded continuation argument
items.note: Continuation proof decomposition; mathematical outline only, no Lean implementation claim.

items.name: Existing integrally closed fraction-ring criterion
items.statement: For commutative R and a fraction ring K, IsIntegrallyClosed R is equivalent to every element of K integral over R being in the image of R. In the geometric use R is a domain and K its fraction field.

items.name: Existing local-ring unit dichotomy
items.statement: In a local ring R, for every e either e or1−e is a unit. A unit idempotent is1. Thus an idempotent in a commutative local ring is0 or1, using e(1−e)=0.

items.name: Existing connected-spectrum idempotent criterion
items.statement: For a nontrivial commutative ring R, Spec R is connected iff every idempotent is0 or1. Connectedness descends along an injective ring map into a ring with connected spectrum.

items.name: Existing scheme-cohomology Euler characteristic
items.statement: For a scheme X over a field k and an O_X-module F, use AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.eulerCharBelow k X F n=Σ_(i<n)(−1)^i dim_k H^i(X,F). For a proper coherent surface sheaf the full Euler characteristic uses n=3, after proving finite-dimensionality and vanishing in degrees at least3.

items.name: Noetherian scheme formal functions from its existing owner
items.statement: For proper f:X→Y with Y locally Noetherian and F coherent, the completed stalk of R^q f_*F at y is the inverse limit of H^q(X_n,F|X_n), where X_n=X×Y Spec(O_Y,y/m_y^n).

items.name: Finite locally free projection formula
items.statement: For a morphism f:X→Y of ringed spaces, finite locally free E on Y and an O_X-module F, the canonical map E⊗R^q f_*F→R^q f_*(f*E⊗F) is an isomorphism for all q≥0.

items.name: Shared Leray spectral sequence
items.statement: For composable scheme structure morphisms T→S→Spec k and a sheaf F in the usual bounded-below sheaf-cohomology setting, use E2^(a,b)=H^a(S,R^b f_*F) converging to H^(a+b)(T,F), with d_r of bidegree(r,1−r).
items.locator: DiamondsAndVStacks:D0 ordinary Leray contract; Stacks02V7 and08AR consumers

items.name: Flat coherent base change for algebraic spaces
items.statement: In a cartesian square of algebraic spaces with f quasi-compact and quasi-separated and base map g flat, quasi-coherent F satisfies g*R^i f_*F≅R^i f′_*g′*F for every i≥0.

items.name: Coherence of proper direct images on algebraic spaces
items.statement: If f:X→Y is proper between algebraic spaces and Y locally Noetherian, then R^i f_*F is coherent for coherent F and every i≥0. No flatness of F over Y is assumed.
items.locator: Stacks08AR, statement and full displayed proof read

items.name: Formal functions on an algebraic space
items.statement: For proper f:X→Y of algebraic spaces, locally Noetherian Y and coherent F, (R^q f_*F)^completed_ybar≅lim_n H^q(X_n,F_n), with the infinitesimal neighbourhoods defined using the strictly henselian étale local ring at ybar.
items.locator: Stacks08AV,08AY,08AZ,08B1; transitive proof engine not fully read

items.name: Relative spectrum in Stein factorization
items.statement: For a proper map f:X→Y of algebraic spaces, form Y′=Spec_Y(f_*O_X). It factors f as h:X→Y′ then π:Y′→Y, with h proper and surjective, π integral, and O_Y′≅h_*O_X canonically. Formation commutes with flat base change.

api.name: Witaszek22.stein_relative_spectrum.algebra
api.statement: The intermediate space is the relative spectrum of f_*O_X with its canonical O_Y-algebra.

api.name: Witaszek22.stein_relative_spectrum.factorization
api.statement: The composite π∘h equals f and O_Y′→h_*O_X is the canonical isomorphism.

api.name: Witaszek22.stein_relative_spectrum.flatBaseChange
api.statement: A flat base change identifies the new intermediate algebra/space and both maps.

items.name: Formal idempotents prove connected geometric fibres
items.statement: For proper f:X→Y of algebraic spaces with Y locally Noetherian and canonical O_Y≅f_*O_X, every geometric fibre is connected.

items.name: Finite Stein factorization over a locally Noetherian base
items.statement: If f:X→Y is proper between algebraic spaces and Y locally Noetherian, stein-relative-spectrum has π finite and h proper with geometrically connected fibres.

items.name: Proper algebraic spaces admit Noetherian approximation
items.statement: A proper morphism X→Y of algebraic spaces with Y qcqs is a cofiltered limit of proper finitely presented X_i→Y_i, where Y_i is of finite presentation over Z and the transition morphisms on sources and targets are affine.

items.name: Proper maps to a normal target preserve functions under generic hypotheses
items.statement: Let f:X→Y be proper between algebraic spaces, with Y normal integral, X reduced, every generic point of X mapping to the generic point η of Y, and H0(X_η,O)=κ(η). Then O_Y≅f_*O_X and f has geometrically connected fibres. In particular this holds for proper birational maps of integral schemes to a normal target.

items.name: Line-bundle sections under a contraction
items.statement: For a proper surjective scheme morphism f:X→Y with canonical O_Y≅f_*O_X and a line bundle L, the canonical pullback isomorphism H0(Y,L^m)≅H0(X,f*L^m) holds for every integer m, compatibly with products and restriction to opens.
items.locator: Stacks01E8 applied to Witaszek contractions and resolution-sections

items.name: Global generation descends when all sections descend
items.statement: Let f:X→Y be a surjective scheme morphism and L a line bundle such that pullback H0(Y,L)→H0(X,f*L) is an isomorphism. Then L is globally generated iff f*L is globally generated.

items.name: Cohomology above the dimension of a Noetherian space
items.statement: For a Noetherian topological space X of dimension at most d and any abelian sheaf F, H^q(X,F)=0 for q>d.

items.name: Higher direct images above the dimension of a proper fibre
items.statement: If f:X→Y is proper with Y locally Noetherian and F coherent, then (R^q f_*F)_y=0 whenever q>dim X_y. In particular fibres of dimension at most1 imply R^q f_*F=0 for q≥2.
items.locator: Stacks02V7, full displayed proof read; broader0E7D also read

items.name: Direct images of a surface resolution
items.statement: For the projective resolution π:T→S in surface-resolution, R1π_*O_T is coherent with finite support and R^qπ_*O_T=0 for q≥2.
items.locator: Explicit supplier decomposition for Witaszek §2 and the surface argument pp700–701

items.name: An invertible twist preserves the length of a finite-support sheaf
items.statement: For a coherent sheaf F supported on finitely many closed points of a Noetherian scheme and an invertible L, length(F_y⊗L_y)=length(F_y) at every support point. No canonical trivialization of L_y is asserted.

items.name: Finite-support coherent sheaves have no higher cohomology
items.statement: For X proper over a field k and coherent F with finite support, H^q(X,F)=0 for q>0 and dim_k H0(X,F)=Σ_y length(F_y)[κ(y):k].

items.name: Leray differential in the surface Euler correction
items.statement: For π:T→S as above over algebraically closed k and L invertible, put Q_m=R1π_*O_T⊗L^m. Besides the H0 isomorphism there is an exact sequence0→H1(S,L^m)→H1(T,π*L^m)→H0(S,Q_m)→H2(S,L^m)→H2(T,π*L^m)→0. The middle arrow is the possibly nonzero d2^(0,1).

items.name: Existing Artin–Rees filtration comparison
items.statement: For a Noetherian commutative ring R, finite R-module M, ideal I and submodule N, there is k such that for n≥k, I^n M∩N=I^(n−k)(I^k M∩N).

items.name: Existing uniform Artin–Rees controlled lift
items.statement: For ideal I and submodule N of a finite module M over a Noetherian commutative ring, there is a shift k0 depending only on I,N such that, for every module surjection φ:P→N and every depth m, an element of N lying in I^(m+k0)M has a φ-preimage in I^m P.

items.name: Existing locality of an adic completion
items.statement: If R is a commutative local ring with finitely generated maximal ideal m, AdicCompletion m R is a local ring. In particular this applies to every Noetherian local R.

items.name: Conjecture 1.9 (statement only)
items.statement: Let M̄_{g,n} be the moduli space of genus-g curves with n marked points over Spec Z, and L a nef line bundle on it. If L is semiample on M̄_{g,n} × Spec Q, then L is semiample. A conjecture the paper states; not proved.
